author: bridget_mccourt
subject: Leaf blower at 7am. Again.
body: It is seven on a Saturday and the leaf blower on Pennock Drive has been going for twenty minutes. The same house did this two weekends ago, and the weekend before that. I am not asking for the police. I am asking for a little mercy and a rake.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Some of us work for a living, and the leaves do not wait for your convenience. Seven is not a crime, Bridget.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Seven on a Saturday is a crime in my book, Ansel, and I have the decibel app to prove it. Maybe the leaves can wait until nine like the rest of us.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: Leaf blowers should be banned before ten and I will die on that hill. Rakes have worked since the Bronze Age.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Nobody asked you, Lloyd. Go complain about someone else's lawn.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Let's all take a breath. Ansel, the blowers are loud for everybody, and Bridget, a polite note to the house usually works better than a post.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Benito, I did send a polite note. It got a shrug and a second blower on Tuesday. I love you, but the polite note has been tried.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Then call the non-emergency line and stop performing for the group chat, Bridget. Nobody on this feed is your jury.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Friendly reminder that many of these blowers belong to crews paid by the hour, so a kind word to the crew supervisor can go a long way. Let's keep it neighborly, please.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Ansel, the non-emergency line is for emergencies, and a blower at seven is not one. Snark is not a noise ordinance, and the town has one.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Leona, you have a whole hobby of ruined roads, so maybe keep your nose out of other people's yard work.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Ansel, your traffic posts have their own parking spot. Maybe park your opinions somewhere else for once.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Okay, enough. Ember Fields is covered by the town nuisance ordinance, and the clerk's office can tell you the quiet hours. Ansel and Bridget, take the rest of it offline.

author: theo_marchetti
subject: New in Wren Hollow: where do you buy groceries, and what is trash day?
body: We moved in this week and I am still finding the cereal in the wrong cabinet. Where do people actually buy groceries around here? Also, what day is trash pickup on our street? The bins have been sitting at the curb since Monday and I don't want to be the new neighbor who misses it.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Welcome to Wren Hollow, Theo! Trash goes out Tuesday, and recycling every other Friday. For bread, Marrow & Yeast Bakehouse on Velder Street is the best on the ridge, and most of us do basics at the big grocery on Tennant Pike.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: Lupe is right about Tuesday trash, Theo. Also join the Tallgrass Ridge Gardeners group, we run a plant swap every April. Welcome, welcome!

comments.author: theo_marchetti
comments.body: Thank you so much! The bakehouse is on my list for Saturday. Is it open on Mondays?

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Closed Mondays, sweetheart, so go Saturday before the cinnamon rolls sell out. For anything with a screw in it, Pruett Hardware & Supply on Cassidy Mill Road is the place.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Welcome, Theo! Come to the creek cleanup on the second Saturday, it's the easiest way to meet people. I'll put your name on the sign-up sheet.

author: ansel_grieco
subject: Fireworks until 1am behind the ball field, again
body: Somebody set off a whole box of illegal fireworks behind the ball field on Fallow Road last night, and they kept going until one in the morning. Dogs were screaming on every street. I don't know who it was, but I know a certain house on Lorimer Court thinks the rules are a suggestion.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Ansel, your posts are like fireworks: loud, bright, and forgotten by Tuesday. Maybe it was the Lorimer Court crew, or maybe a squirrel with a lighter.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Your puns are the only fireworks in this thread, Kwame, and they fizzle. My dog hid under the bed for three hours.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Ansel, I'm not saying it was me. I'm also not saying it wasn't. Your post has more capital letters than the box had rockets.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Let's keep to the facts. The town code treats unpermitted fireworks as a nuisance, and the police non-emergency line takes reports with the time and the address.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Thank you, Deb. Finally somebody who reads the code. Kwame, take notes.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Ansel, I'd take notes if you ever wrote a sentence shorter than a court filing. Deb, nice fact check.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Gentlemen, the ball field is quiet again, and so should this thread be. Ansel, the patrol that covers Fallow Road is nearest most nights, so a call with the time and address is the useful move.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Benito, I did call. It took forty minutes and they said it was probably a wedding. It was not a wedding, Benito.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Ansel, the dispatcher's wedding theory is a fine guess. The Lorimer Court crew does not own a wedding, so put the pitchfork down.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Kwame, your jokes have run out of batteries, and so has my patience.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Ansel, Kwame, both of you, stop. Put the time and address into the non-emergency line, and leave the Lorimer Court families out of this.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: You're right, Deb. Ansel, I'm sorry about your dog. The next quiet night is on me.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Fine. Apology accepted, I suppose.

author: walt_gerrity
subject: Sunrise over the north field
body: Got up early to walk the dog, and the fog was sitting on the north field like it was waiting for somebody to notice. The old fence line lit up gold just as the sun cleared the silo. I have lived on this road since 1990 and I still stop to look.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Walt, that light! Your dog looks thrilled to be in the picture. Did you get one of the fog along the road too?

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Gorgeous. I'll say it twice since I'm bilingual: hermoso. That fence line is exactly what I needed to see on a dreary morning.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: Fiona, the dog is my fault. He thinks every sunrise is a bread crumb. The road shot is the second photo.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: This field is lovely. If anyone needs a ride to the clinic this week, message me, I'm driving Tuesday and Thursday.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: Kofi, I'll take you up on it Thursday. My knees are not what they were at the diner.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: I'm still pretty new here, I moved in a couple of weeks ago, and this is the first photo I've wanted to save. Thank you for posting it.

author: dale_hartwell
subject: A car across the sidewalk on Ashby Lane for three days
body: The gray hatchback parked across the sidewalk on Ashby Lane, right in front of the bus stop, has been there since Thursday. I had to step into the street with my granddaughter's stroller. Parking goes on the road, not on the pavement. Does anyone know whose it is?

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: That is hard with a stroller. Please check with the car owner first, there is often a simple reason like a dead battery. Thank you for raising it.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Call the non-emergency line and give them the plate. Parking across a walk is a town ordinance issue and they will tag it.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Thanks, Tomasz. Already did. They said the car has been reported twice and they are 'working on it.'

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Dale, if you can see which house the car belongs to, a knock on the door works more often than people expect.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: I'll knock. I'm not going to be happy about it.

author: sadie_kimbrough
subject: New to Calloway Bluffs, asking about schools for a six-year-old
body: We just moved here for my husband's job, and our daughter starts first grade in January. Which elementary schools do people like? Is walking or the bus the norm for Calloway? Any good after-school tutor would help too. Thank you in advance, I'm excited about this whole town!

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Welcome to Calloway, Sadie. Most kids here walk or take the bus to the elementary school, which is about fifteen minutes on foot from most of the bluffs. Ladder Tutoring Works on Brisco Avenue gets good words from the parents I know.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: Hi neighbor! Our school got a new principal this summer, and the moms I talk to say the first-grade teachers are wonderful. Welcome, welcome!

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Sadie, the school board agendas are posted on the district site, and the attendance boundary map is in the June packet if you want to confirm your address. That is the place to check, not the rumor mill.

comments.author: sadie_kimbrough
comments.body: Thank you, Wendell. That's exactly what I needed. I'll look at the boundary map tonight.

comments.author: noel_brandvold
comments.body: Hi Sadie, I'm new too. I moved to Greaves Mill about two weeks ago. Welcome to the Ridge! I'd also check the library story hour, my son loves it.

author: owen_pruitt
subject: Party on Sorrel Court until 2am, and the bus had to wait
body: The house at the end of Sorrel Court had a party with a DJ until after two this morning. My kids have the bus at 7:10, and the driver had to wait while two cars were moved out of the turnaround. I'm not against fun, but we agreed to quiet hours, and they are in the ordinance.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: Owen, a party until two is not a crime. Some of us are up at that hour because we work nights, and a DJ is not an emergency.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Cyrus, your night owl hours are not my problem, and the bus driver doesn't care that you're up. Two cars blocked the turnaround.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: Owen, you are the most miserable excuse for a neighbor on this block, and your own kids are the only ones who can stand you.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: This is Rosalind Vance. The moderators have removed one comment above. Let us keep to the quiet hours ordinance and the bus turnaround, which the district office can address.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Thank you, Rosalind. The turnaround is the real issue. Cyrus can keep his party and his insults to himself.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Hey all, I'm a young dad with a 2yo who sleeps throuh nothing, so I get it, Owen. Cyrus, you're right it's not a crime though. Maybe they just had a birthday?

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: Owen, call whoever you like about the turnaround. I'm not going to argue about it in front of the bus stop.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: The bus stop has had two near misses this month, Cyrus. I'll call the district tomorrow, and you can stay up and watch me do it.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Hi everyone, I'm a teacher's aide. Please keep the bus in mind, because the kids are the important part of this. Owen, the district transportation number is on the school website under the bus page.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: Good luck with the district, Owen. Sorry for my earlier comment, that was out of line.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Apology noted, Cyrus. Next time skip the name-calling and we'll get along fine.

author: priya_lakhani
subject: Thank you to whoever turned in my wallet at Penrose Lane Books
body: I left my wallet on a shelf in the poetry section one Saturday and didn't notice until I was home. Someone handed it in to the desk with everything still inside, including the cash and my kids' library cards. I don't know who you are, but thank you. I'm baking the cookies I owe you.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: Priya, what a lovely story! The desk staff at Penrose Lane are the best, and I'm so glad it came back with everything inside.

comments.author: colleen_brandt
comments.body: Priya, this made my whole morning! Thank you, Penrose Lane Books, and thank you to whoever turned it in. Everyone, hug your neighbors today!

comments.author: otis_whitfield
comments.body: the desk lady at penrose is a good egg. handed mine in last year too. this town still has some decent people in it.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Priya, I'd tell you to check your wallet twice, but I think the cookies are the real payment. Pun-ishing, I know.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Kwame, you'll have to settle the cookie debt yourself. Thank you all!

author: leona_brooks
subject: Trash cans out on the curb all week on Haddon Court
body: The cans at the end of Haddon Court have been sitting at the curb since last Tuesday, lids open, and the wind keeps spreading bags across the storm drain. I asked nicely once. Garbage day is Tuesday, folks, and it is not a suggestion.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Call the hauler's customer line and give them the address. If the cans were missed, they'll tag them, and that gets somebody's attention faster than a post.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Wade, I did that. The hauler says it's the resident's responsibility. Which resident, Wade? I'm one of the residents.

comments.author: nadia_sorokina
comments.body: I walk my dogs past there every morning. The blue house has renters who moved in about a month ago, so a kind note under the door might head off a fight.

comments.author: frances_hollis
comments.body: A note sounds lovely, Nadia. I'd also check whether the hauler changed its route days this spring. The town calendar lists them under utilities.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Frances, I checked the calendar. The schedule has not changed. Nadia, I'm delighted about your walks, though.

author: dorothy_breen
subject: Hi, I'm new in Millrace. Is there a knitting or book group?
body: Sorry if this is the wrong place to ask. I moved here this week and I don't know anyone yet. Is there a knitting circle or a book group that meets in Millrace Commons? I'd love to find people who want to talk about something other than the weather. Thank you.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: Welcome to Millrace, Dorothy. This is Rosalind Vance. The reading room has a Thursday book group, and the church on Brindle Road hosts a knitting circle on Wednesdays. Penrose Lane Books also runs a Tuesday book club that is far less serious.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Dorothy, welcome! My kids love the Saturday craft morning in the community room. You're not bothering anyone by asking here, we all started out new once.

comments.author: dorothy_breen
comments.body: Thank you so much, Rosalind. I'll look up Thursdays. Is the reading room open to everyone?

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: It is, Dorothy. Simply sign the guest book at the front desk. Welcome again, from Rosalind Vance.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: Welcome, Dorothy! I'm more of a hammer person than a knitter, but if anything in the house needs a hand, ask. Pruett Hardware & Supply on Cassidy Mill Road will sort out most of what you'll need.

author: tomasz_wojcik
subject: Barking dog on Tollgate Court, every night since August
body: The dog two lots down on Tollgate Court barks from ten at night until well past midnight, every single night for six weeks. I talked to the owner last month and nothing changed. I'm up at five for work and I'm done being polite about it.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Earplugs are cheaper than a lawyer, Tomasz. Also, has anyone on this feed checked whether the dog is barking at a squirrel?

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Dale, Tomasz didn't ask for earplug advice. He asked for a quiet night, and the town nuisance ordinance covers barking after ten.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Leona, you complain about the roads more than the roads complain about you. Maybe the dog is the only one on your side.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Dale, I'd rather complain about roads than sit in a truck waiting for a spot on Ashby Lane. Some of us can count.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Okay, both of you, let's bring it down. Tomasz, the Ridge Dog Owners Circle can send a quiet-hours reminder to the dog owners on your block. That is concrete, and better than a shouting match.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Please do. I'd take a reminder over a lecture. Thanks, Imani.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Imani, a reminder is fine, but I've never seen one stop a bark. Tomasz should buy a white noise machine.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Dale, you have never once had a dog bark at your house at midnight, so spare us the white noise advice.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Two of you are fighting over a dog, and the dog is winning. Someone bring the bones.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Leona, I'm done with this. Tomasz, call the owner once more, then the non-emergency line, and keep a dated log.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Dale, the non-emergency line has a long voicemail queue. Tomasz, the town's complaint form on its website logs the dates, which helps when you need it.

author: kwame_ofori
subject: Our raccoon has a better filing system than the city
body: A raccoon has been sorting my recycling for a week, and I swear he is getting better at it. Here is one photo of him sitting in the blue bin like it's a hot tub. My wife says he is a tenant now, and I have stopped arguing.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Kwame, if he's staying, get bins with latches. The county site has the link to the free lid program under wildlife.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Raccoons can carry roundworm, so keep the bins lidded and don't let the kids near him. Otherwise I agree, he is a very fine raccoon.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Deb, the raccoon has been informed. He has no interest in roundworm, only in my cheese.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: I carried mail on this route for thirty years, and raccoons were always the real route supervisors. This one is a tenant, Kwame, and his lease is at your curb.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: Kwame, the folks at the pizza place on Tennant Pike said he came in for a slice last month. Is that true?
